Chris —

Appreciate the quick review and the redlines. TL;DR answers below, details and proposed language follow. Happy to hop on a 30-min sync.

- Standard uptime commitment: We propose a baseline of 99.95% for hosted inference endpoints.
- Monthly service credits: sliding bands — availability >= 99.95% (no credit); 99.5–99.95% (2% monthly credit); 99.0–99.5% (6%); <99.0% (12%), with a monthly cap of 50% of fees for the impacted service.
- Temporary exemptions: We can formalize a "planned-exception" pathway. Requests must be submitted in writing at least 14 business days in advance, include start/end windows, rollback plan, expected impact to availability/latency, and an acceptance by both parties. If accepted, the affected window is excluded from remedy calculations.
- Latency SLOs: We treat latency separately. Latency degradations (p95 > agreed threshold for two or more consecutive days) can trigger a separate credit pool; they do not double-count with availability credits.

Proposed language excerpt (for the SLA redline):
• Availability bands and monthly remedy cap (50% of monthly invoice for the impacted product line).
• Formal Planned Exception Procedure: 14 business days notice + migration runbook + mutually agreed carveout.
• Latency remediation: p95-based thresholds, independent credit pool, escalates to joint RCA if observed >3x in a 30-day window.

I'll attach a draft clause we can drop into your PDF and copy in OpsGrid legal. If that looks good we can turn it into a tracked redline.

Thanks,

Chris / OpsGrid Legal —

Attached is the tracked-ready clause (EdgeFin_SLA_redline_v3.pdf updated). Key points we updated per feedback:
- Baseline uptime commitment: 99.95%.
- Availability credit bands: >=99.95% = 0%; 99.5–99.95% = 2%; 99.0–99.5% = 6%; <99.0% = 12%.
- Monthly aggregate remedy cap: 50% of the applicable monthly fees (this cap applies across availability and latency credits; remedies are not additive beyond 50%).
- Planned Exception Process: written request at least 14 business days in advance, include start/end, rollback plan, expected impact; default max duration per exception = 5 days (can be extended by mutual written agreement). Exception windows accepted by both parties are excluded from remedy calculations.
- Latency SLOs: handled via a separate credit pool; latency credits are subject to the same aggregate cap and will not be double-counted with availability credits.
